newsitem.title: USA: Top Chinese backed plan to buy favor - report.
newsitem.headline: Top Chinese backed plan to buy favor - report.

text.p: The FBI has obtained substantial evidence that "top" Chinese officials approved plans in 1995 to attempt to buy influence with U.S. politicians and that the scheme continued through the 1996 elections, the Washington Post reported on Friday.

The newspaper, quoting unidentified U.S. government officials, said secret communications between Beijing and the Chinese Embassy in Washington established that the influence-buying plan was "government sanctioned."
"There is today ongoing pressure to keep going, despite the (campaign finance) investigation and press attention," another unnamed source told the Post.

The officials declined to name the Chinese leaders who allegedly approved the plans. "It's a pretty small top," one source said, noting that the number one official in China is President Jiang Zemin and the number two is Premier Li Peng.

The Post reported that while officials said the FBI now had what one described as "amazing" detail showing the Chinese intent to buy influence, and has tracked some China-U.S. money transfers they believed may be connected, investigatorts had not tied that information to any payment to an individual or an organization.

FBI Director Louis Freeh and Attorney General Janet Reno briefed senior members of the Senate Intelligence Committee about the establishment of a connection between the scheme and the highest levels of the Chinese government, according to the newspaper.
